sentence: This project builds an imaging system that attaches to the head of a rodent and moves with it to record neural activity while it explores.
This project studies how cadmium exposure disrupts the repair of DNA double-strand breaks and promotes triple-negative breast cancer.
This project studies how the brain represents the incentive value of cues and how brain circuits use those cues to drive motivated behavior.
This project studies why infants born preterm, after oxygen exposure at birth, are more vulnerable to worse respiratory infections and wheezing later in life.
This project studies why colorectal cancer occurs and causes death more often in some populations across the US than in others.
This project studies how genetic defects change how the thyroid works and tests gene therapy plus a thyroid hormone analogue as a preclinical treatment.
This project builds technologies that help explain the biochemical and physical basis of disease and its diagnosis.
This project studies how glycolysis and acetyl-CoA metabolism affect immune activation and epigenetic changes as cells change fate, using a mouse model.
This project studies how paraventricular thalamic circuits contribute to opioid withdrawal and heroin seeking.
This project studies how brain network connections and genetic factors affect the spread of tau pathology in early-onset Alzheimer's disease, using brain imaging.
This project provides genomic and bioinformatics services and sequencing instruments for a wide range of genomic studies.
This project tests a cell therapy using type 1 conventional dendritic cells to boost immune responses against tumors and improve response to immune checkpoint blockade.
This project studies how progesterone, allopregnanolone and estrogen affect hippocampal plasticity and function after early life adversity.
This project makes nanoplastics that resemble those in the environment and studies how they interact with environmental contaminants and biomolecules to cause toxic effects.
This project builds fiber-coupled microendoscopes that image tissue and neuron activity in living animals in real time.
This project uses a wearable device to measure how close children stay to their caregivers and how that relates to brain development in infants.
This project studies how hydrogen sulfide exposure makes mice more likely to get severe lung infection from influenza A virus.
This project builds tools to find out what cancer-associated microproteins do in cancer.
This project tests whether virus-like particles that display peanut peptide antigens, with immune adjuvants, safely treat peanut allergy in mouse models.
This project tests whether blocking the protein lysyl oxidase helps triple negative breast cancer overcome resistance to chemotherapy.
